subject: PRN
body: How many principles does PRINCE2 7 have?
explanation: There are seven principles, seven practices and seven processes.

subject: PRN
body: In PRINCE2 7, the seven 'themes' of earlier editions are now called
explanation: PRINCE2 7 renamed themes to practices.

subject: PRN
body: Which practice is NOT one of the seven PRINCE2 7 practices?
explanation: The practices are business case, organizing, plans, quality, risk, issues and progress.

subject: PRN
body: Which are the five integrated elements of PRINCE2 7?
options: Initiation, planning, delivery, control and closure
Plans, risks, issues, stages and reports
Principles, people, practices, processes and the project context
Time, cost, scope, quality and risk
explanation: PRINCE2 7 added 'people' and 'project context' as integrated elements.

subject: PRN
body: Who owns the business case?
explanation: The executive is accountable for the project and owns the business case.

subject: PRN
body: Which role is accountable for specifying the benefits and ensuring they are realized?
explanation: The senior user represents those who will use the products.

subject: PRN
body: Which three roles make up the project board?
options: Executive, senior user and senior supplier
Project manager, team manager and project support
Executive, project manager and team manager
explanation: The project board directs the project.

subject: PRN
body: Which process is used by the project board throughout the project?
explanation: It runs from the end of starting up to project closure.

subject: PRN
body: Which process produces the project brief?
explanation: Starting up a project happens before the project formally begins.

subject: PRN
body: Which process produces the project initiation documentation (PID)?
explanation: The PID forms the 'contract' between the project manager and project board.

subject: PRN
body: Which process is mainly carried out by the team manager?
explanation: The team manager accepts, executes and delivers work packages.

subject: PRN
body: What is a work package?
options: A set of information about one or more products, agreed between the project manager and team manager
The final report on the project
The project board's approval to start the project
explanation: Work packages are authorized in controlling a stage.

subject: PRN
body: What is the minimum number of management stages in a PRINCE2 project?
options: Two: an initiation stage and at least one further stage
explanation: The initiation stage is always the first management stage.

subject: PRN
body: Who sets project-level tolerances?
options: The business layer (corporate, programme or customer management)
explanation: The project board sets stage tolerances; the project manager sets work package tolerances.

subject: PRN
body: Who sets stage tolerances?
explanation: The project board delegates authority to the project manager within stage tolerances.

subject: PRN
body: Who sets work package tolerances?
explanation: Team managers must escalate if work package tolerances are forecast to be exceeded.

subject: PRN
body: What should the project manager produce if stage tolerances are forecast to be exceeded?
explanation: The board may then request an exception plan.

subject: PRN
body: Which of these is a tolerance area in PRINCE2 7?
explanation: Tolerance areas include time, cost, scope, quality, benefits, risk and sustainability.

subject: PRN
body: Which risk response is appropriate only for threats?
explanation: Exploit and enhance are opportunity responses; share applies to both.

subject: PRN
body: Which risk response is appropriate only for opportunities?
explanation: Avoid, reduce, fallback and transfer are threat responses.

subject: PRN
body: Which response applies to both threats and opportunities?
explanation: Share and accept/prepare contingent plans can apply to both.

subject: PRN
body: Which of these is a type of issue in PRINCE2?
explanation: Issue types: request for change, off-specification, problem/concern.

subject: PRN
body: An off-specification is
options: something that should be provided by the project but currently is (or is forecast to be) not provided
a change requested by a user
explanation: Off-specifications are a type of issue.

subject: PRN
body: Which plan is optional in PRINCE2?
explanation: Team plans are produced at the team manager's discretion.

subject: PRN
body: Which plan replaces a stage or project plan after an exception?
explanation: It shows how to recover from the effect of the deviation.

subject: PRN
body: What does product-based planning start with?
explanation: Then create the product breakdown structure, product descriptions and product flow diagram.

subject: PRN
body: What does a product flow diagram show?
options: The sequence in which products are developed and their dependencies
explanation: It follows the product breakdown structure.

subject: PRN
body: In a quality review, who is responsible for the product being reviewed?
explanation: Quality review roles: chair, presenter, reviewer, administrator.

subject: PRN
body: Where are the results of quality activities recorded?
explanation: It provides a record of planned and completed quality activities.

subject: PRN
body: Which log is the project manager's diary for informal issues and actions?
explanation: Informal issues can be handled in the daily log.

subject: PRN
body: Which document describes the purpose, composition and quality criteria of a product?
explanation: Product descriptions are created during planning.

subject: PRN
body: The business case is first outlined in which process?
explanation: It is detailed during initiating a project and updated at stage boundaries.

subject: PRN
body: What are the three tests of business justification in PRINCE2?
explanation: The project must remain desirable, viable and achievable.

subject: PRN
body: Benefits are usually realized
explanation: The benefits management approach covers post-project reviews.

subject: PRN
body: Which principle is supported by setting tolerances?
explanation: Tolerances allow delegation without constant escalation.

subject: PRN
body: Which principle means a project should stop if it can no longer be justified?
explanation: If justification lapses, the project should be closed prematurely.

subject: PRN
body: Which role cannot be shared or delegated?
explanation: There is only one executive, ensuring single-point accountability.

subject: PRN
body: Can the project manager and executive be the same person?
explanation: These roles must remain separate.

subject: PRN
body: What does 'tailoring' PRINCE2 mean?
options: Adapting the method to suit the project's context
Removing the principles you don't need
explanation: The principles must always be applied; tailoring adapts everything else.

subject: PRN
body: What is configuration management concerned with?
options: Identifying, tracking and protecting the project's products and their versions
explanation: Configuration item records and product status accounts support it.

subject: PRN
body: What happens in 'managing a stage boundary'?
options: The current stage is reviewed, the next stage is planned and the business case is updated
explanation: It provides the project board with information to authorize the next stage.

subject: PRN
body: PRINCE2 7 places new emphasis on
explanation: PRINCE2 7 added a 'people' element and sustainability as a performance target.

subject: PRN
body: How many marks are needed to pass the PRINCE2 7 Foundation exam?
explanation: 60 questions in 60 minutes, closed book.
